title: A Brunn-Minkowski Theory for the Distribution of Random Pairs of Points in Convex Bodies
summary: Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body, let $X$ and $Y$ be independent uniform points of $K$, and set $R_K=(|K|/ω_n)^{1/n}$. We consider the distribution function \[ D_K(ρ)=\mathbb P\{|X-Y|/R_K<ρ\}, \] and its homogeneous counterpart \begin{equation*} \mathcal J_ρ(K)=\iint_{K\times K}\mathbf{1}_{\{|x-y|<ρR_K\}}dxdy. \end{equation*} Thus $D_K(ρ)$ is the proportion of ordered pairs of points of $K$ whose distance is less than $ρR_K$, or equivalently the radial distribution function of the normalized covariogram of $K$.
